name: revision_2026-10-02
status: written before either analysis below was run; the canonical results it builds on were already known, so both analyses are post hoc revision sensitivities, not confirmatory tests

R1_delay_at_strict_budget.question: Does the ordering at delta=0.01 survive delayed actuation?
R1_delay_at_strict_budget.data: 200 verified Alibaba services, days 0-9 history, days 10-12 test

policies.B6: conformal margin + fixed +1 offset (h=2, rho=0.70), alpha in {1,1.25,1.5,2}
policies.B7: conformal margin only, alpha in {1,1.25,1.5,2} (alpha=1 primary)
policies.reactive_cal1pct: threshold/cooldown selected per service on days 8-9 at a 1% calibration budget (primary reactive comparator)
policies.reactive_cal0.25pct: same rule at a 0.25% calibration budget (retrospective comparator from Table 2)

R1_delay_at_strict_budget.semantics: closed-loop FIFO queue as in Additional file 1 Sect. S8: decision at t applied at t+tau; offset trigger uses realised overload/soft state under applied capacity; initial queue filled with the last observed capacity
metrics: mean and median relative replay cost vs observed capacity
same for the upper pre-test-size quartile (Q4, 50 services)
R1_delay_at_strict_budget.regression_check: tau=0 must reproduce Table 2: B6 alpha=1 199/200 at mean 0.4478; B7 alpha=1 197/200 at 0.4440; reactive_cal1pct 190/200 at 0.4355; reactive_cal0.25pct 197/200 at 0.4429. If not, stop and report the discrepancy.

R2_extended_reactive_grid.question: Is the reactive comparator handicapped by the lower end of its threshold grid?
R2_extended_reactive_grid.selection_rule: unchanged: per unit, calibration-feasible minimum relative cost, ties by overload, decreasing threshold, increasing cooldown; if none feasible, minimum calibration overload then cost

datasets.alibaba200: calibration = train -> days 8-9, test = days 0-9 -> days 10-12; relative cost vs observed capacity (recompute_reactive_baseline.reactive_capacity/metrics)
datasets.huawei2023_primary: as external_replication_2026_09_30.replay_reactive; relative cost vs clairvoyant capacity

R2_extended_reactive_grid.implementation_note: the external reactive kernel is evaluated with a time-stepped NumPy vectorisation over units and configurations (numba unavailable); equivalence is checked by reproducing every original-grid row of per_unit_*_primary.csv.gz
R2_extended_reactive_grid.regression_check: original grid must reproduce: Alibaba 190/200 (1%) and 198/200 (5%); Huawei 47/64 and Azure 1123/2839 at 1%; 1562 Azure applications calibration-infeasible at 1%.
R2_extended_reactive_grid.reporting_rule: results are reported whatever their direction; the paper keeps the protocol-fixed original-grid comparator as primary and reports the extended grid as a sensitivity, revising claims if the extended comparator changes the ordering

R3_horizon_aligned_addendum.status: added after the R1 results were seen (R1 showed that B6 at alpha=1 loses compliance under delay); written before R3 was run
R3_horizon_aligned_addendum.question: Does calibrating the margin on the residual of the horizon actually controlled restore the strict-budget behaviour under delay without inflating alpha?
R3_horizon_aligned_addendum.policy: with delay tau the decision made after observing d_{t-1} is applied at step t+tau, so the score is the (tau+1)-step persistence residual e^+_j = max(d_j - d_{j-tau-1}, 0); the margin is the corrected rank l_W(delta) of the last W such scores observable at decision time; nominal capacity ceil(d_{t-1} + margin); offset and queue semantics as in R1
R3_horizon_aligned_addendum.regression_check: tau=0 (h=1) must reproduce B6 199/200 at 0.4478 and B7 197/200 at 0.4440 exactly
R3_horizon_aligned_addendum.theory_note: Proposition 5.1 applies to the (tau+1)-step score under its exchangeability assumption; overlapping multi-step residuals are more strongly dependent, so the assumption is weaker in practice

R4_external_delay_addendum.status: written after R1-R3 had been seen, before R4 was run; requested to test whether the strict-budget advantage on the two external traces survives actuation delay
R4_external_delay_addendum.data: Huawei 2023 (64 functions, mu_p50) and Azure Functions 2019 (2,839 applications, K=10), primary capacity units, test days as in the external replication

policies.B6: conformal W=240 margin + offset (rho=0.70, gamma=1, h=2), alpha in {1, 2}
policies.B6-h / B7-h: margin calibrated on the (tau+1)-step persistence residual max(d_j - d_{j-tau-1}, 0), alpha=1
policies.reactive_cal_orig: per-unit threshold/cooldown selected on days 8-9 at the same budget, original grid u>=0.5 (protocol comparator)
policies.reactive_cal_ext: same with the extended grid u>=0.2 (R2)
policies.reactive_cal_ext_strict: extended grid selected at a calibration budget of delta/4 (0.25% or 1.25%), the analogue of the retrospective strict reactive on Alibaba

R4_external_delay_addendum.semantics: closed-loop FIFO queue: the decision computed after observing d_{t-1} is applied at step t+tau; the offset trigger uses soft-utilisation states under applied capacity, exactly as the canonical guarded() at tau=0. Margin policies start warm: the first tau applied capacities are the decisions the same rule makes on the last tau pre-test minutes. Reactive policies start with their canonical initial capacity max(1, ceil(d/(0.8 mu))) in the queue.
R4_external_delay_addendum.cost: total replay cost relative to the clairvoyant capacity, as in the external replication
R4_external_delay_addendum.regression_check: tau=0 must reproduce the stored B6 (alpha 1 and 2) and B7 overload counts and relative costs of per_unit_*_primary.csv.gz, and the stored R2 reactive test rows, exactly; otherwise stop
R4_external_delay_addendum.reporting_rule: reported whatever the direction; primary contrast is B6 vs reactive_cal_orig and B6-h vs reactive_cal_ext_strict at tau=1

R5_alibaba_delay_symmetric_addendum.status: written after R1-R4 had been seen, before R5 was run; completes the Alibaba delay design so that the three traces are reported with identical policies and budgets
R5_alibaba_delay_symmetric_addendum.policies: B6 (alpha 1, 2), B7, B6-h, B7-h, reactive_cal_orig, reactive_cal_ext, reactive_cal_ext_strict (calibration budget delta/4), definitions as in R4; queue semantics as in R1
R5_alibaba_delay_symmetric_addendum.regression_check: delta=0.01 rows must reproduce R1/R3; delta=0.05 B6 alpha 1 and 2 must reproduce the stored closed_loop_delay_per_service.csv of Additional file 1 Sect. S8 at all tau

R6_pac_rank_addendum.status: written after R1-R5 had been seen, before R6 was run
R6_pac_rank_addendum.question: Does a training-conditional (PAC) rank, which targets per-window coverage rather than marginal coverage, give high per-unit compliance without the heuristic offset or alpha inflation, alone and combined with horizon-aligned scores?
R6_pac_rank_addendum.rank_rule: l_PAC(W, delta, eta) = smallest l with P(Bin(W, 1-delta) >= l) <= eta; under i.i.d. scores the conditional miscoverage of the l-th order statistic exceeds delta with probability at most eta (Vovk 2012); ties only make it conservative
R6_pac_rank_addendum.window_rule: primary W = smallest W in {240, 480, 960, 1440, 2880} for which an unsaturated PAC rank (l <= W-1) exists: W=480, l=479 at delta=1%; W=240, l=234 at delta=5%. Secondary: W=1440 at both budgets (l=1433 and l=1382). Fixed from (delta, eta) only, before any data are replayed.

policies.B7-PAC: PAC margin only (no offset, alpha=1), primary W; horizon-aligned (tau+1)-step scores when tau>0

R6_pac_rank_addendum.comparators: B6, B6-h, B7, reactive B1 and the strict extended-grid reactive from R4/R5 (not re-run)
R6_pac_rank_addendum.regression_check: the generic simulator with the conformal rank at W=240 must reproduce stored B7 at tau=0 and B7-h at tau=1 exactly on every trace

R7_round2_addendum.status: written after R1-R6 and the second external review had been seen, before R7 was run

parts.pac_grid: B7-PAC (margin only, no offset) for W in {240,480,960,1440,2880} (only W with an unsaturated PAC rank are used), eta in {0.05,0.10,0.20}, delta in {1%,5%}, tau in {0,1,5}; for tau>0 both horizon-aligned (tau+1)-step scores and one-step scores (ablation for horizon alignment)
parts.window_selection: pre-test rule per trace and budget: replay B7-PAC (eta=0.05, tau=0, one-step scores) on calibration days 8-9 with the preceding days as history for every admissible W; choose the W with the most units within budget on the calibration days, ties broken by lower mean calibration cost; the choice is then evaluated once on the test days
parts.conservativeness: mean realised overload and budget utilisation (overload fraction / delta: mean and median) for B7-PAC, B6-h and the strict reactive comparator
parts.martingales: conformal test martingale per unit on the test-period one-step positive persistence residuals (and (tau+1)=2-step residuals): conformal p-values with random tie-breaking (seed 20261002), simple-mixture power martingale over epsilon in (0,1); reject exchangeability at level 0.01 when the running maximum reaches 100 (Ville). Reported for the full test sequence and for non-overlapping blocks of 240 steps

R7_round2_addendum.regression_check: pac_grid rows with eta=0.05 and horizon-aligned scores at W in {480/240, 1440} must reproduce R6 exactly

R8_confirmatory.status: frozen before any policy was replayed on these data; at freezing time the R7 grid and martingale runs were still in progress and their results had not been inspected
R8_confirmatory.data: Huawei Cloud 2023 private trace, contiguous runs not used by any earlier analysis: trace days 0-18 (run A), 147-165 (run B), 168-184 (run C). Per run: relative days 0-7 history, 8-9 calibration, the rest test (9, 9, 7 days). Units and capacity units selected on relative days 0-7 with the rule of the external replication (57, 67, 71 functions). The functions overlap with those of the earlier replication; the time periods do not.
R8_confirmatory.proposed_method: margin-only PAC rank, eta=0.05, horizon-aligned (tau+1)-step persistence scores, no offset, no alpha; W chosen per run and budget by the R7 pre-test rule on calibration days 8-9 (most units within budget at tau=0 with one-step scores, ties by lower mean cost) among admissible W in {240,480,960,1440,2880}
R8_confirmatory.comparators: B6 and B6-h (W=240 conformal rank, offset), reactive B1 (original grid, calibration budget delta), strict reactive (grid u>=0.2, calibration budget delta/4), all selected on calibration days 8-9

hypotheses.H1_primary: at delta=1% and tau=1, pooled over the three runs (unit x run), the proposed method keeps more units within budget than the strict reactive controller; exact one-sided paired sign test on discordant units, alpha=0.05
hypotheses.H2: the proposed method keeps at least 95% of pooled units within budget at every (delta, tau) in the design
hypotheses.H3_descriptive: ratio of mean relative replay cost, proposed over strict reactive, reported without a directional hypothesis

R8_confirmatory.reporting_rule: all hypotheses and all cells are reported whatever their outcome; any deviation from this protocol is recorded in this entry

R9_round3_addendum.status: written after the third external review, before R9 was run; sensitivity analyses only, the primary rule and the frozen R8 protocol are unchanged
R9_round3_addendum.stride_pac: PAC rank applied to the stride-(tau+1) subsequence of the window: the W_eff = floor(W/(tau+1)) most recent non-overlapping (tau+1)-step scores (s = t, t-tau-1, ...), rank l_PAC(W_eff, delta, eta=0.05); with i.i.d. one-step increments these scores and the covered score are i.i.d., so Corollary 5.3 applies. Evaluated for W in {960,1440,2880}, tau in {1,5}, delta in {1%,5%}, only where an unsaturated rank exists, on the three main traces and the three confirmatory Huawei periods; compared with the overlapping-score PAC-h at the same W
R9_round3_addendum.cost_aware_window_rule: sensitivity rule: among admissible W, choose the cheapest on calibration days 8-9 among those keeping at least 99% of units within budget there (eta=0.05, tau=0, one-step scores); evaluated on the test days at tau in {0,1,5}; requires overlapping PAC-h at all admissible W, which R7 provides for the main traces and R9 computes for the confirmatory periods
